text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Education Minister Teo Chee Hean spells out his vision of how Singapore's education system would have to change because world itself changing rapidly.
- There have been some "encouraging developments" in Singapore-Malaysia relations since June, Foreign Minister S Jayakumar says in Parliament.
- United States considers Pol Pot war criminal and wants him to face trial.
- New global initiative to attract much-needed foreign talent to Singapore launched, with centres set up in six cities to offer information on working, studying and living conditions.

- Singapore Technologies Telemedia eyeing second, and possibly even third, telecommunications satellite project which will be "similar in size" to its Singapore $937.6 million Asia-Pacific Mobile Telecommunications project in 1995.
- Two Indonesian consortia apply for licences to supply electricity to Singapore from separate 500-megawatt power stations on Batam, says Public Utilities Board.
- Singapore's moves to support Thai baht when first came under speculative attack in mid-May do not seem to have cost country yet as latest data show official foreign reserves still rising.

- Japan's Ministry of Finance announces severe penalties against country's leading brokerage Nomura Securities and major commercial bank Dai-Ichi Kangyo for illicit dealings with sokaiya corporate extortionists.
- Several property buyers and BT readers blast developers for urging government to curb land sales.
- IPC Corp more than triples its interim net profit to S$18.8 million, beating analysts' full-year estimates of S$15.7 million.
- It's half-time, and analysts predict interim profits growth of 12 to 18 percent for Big Four banks, with OUB leading pack.
- Indonesia's government gives its blessing to sale of Salim Group subsidiary PT Indofood Sukses Makmur to Singapore's QAF Ltd, saying deal would add 1.7 trillion rupiah to its coffers.
- Vietnamese businessman suing local cigarette manufacturer Rothmans of Pall Mall (Singapore) for breach of contract.
- Newly-listed Asia Food & Properties will be facing uphill task in its bid to sell another S$367.5 million in new shares to new investors.
